The chart app calls `reportError` in three places, all in two files. Each call sits inside an error path, so a behaviour change would surface as a change in how these hooks report failures.

1. **`useOrderableConceptSets`** (`openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/orders/useOrderableConceptSets.ts`, lines 71–75): an effect calls `reportError(error)` when the SWR fetch fails. The hook is exported and consumed by the orders UI.
2. **`useOrderableConceptSWR`** (same file, lines 34–38): a second effect calls `reportError(error)` on the SWR error. It runs on every render, without a dependency array.
3. **`useFavoritesActions`** (`openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/order-favorites/useFavoritesActions.ts`, line 57): `persistFavorites` calls `reportError(error)` in its `catch`, alongside a error snackbar. `deleteMultipleFavorites` relies on it.

The framework side is `reportError` in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-error-handling/src/index.ts` (lines 56–61). It is re-exported through `@openmrs/esm-framework` (`packages/framework/esm-framework/src/index.ts`, line 6). It currently throws the normalised error inside `setTimeout`, so `window.onerror` displays it as a toast. Any change to that timing, normalisation or toast routing would affect the three call sites above.

I did not search for downstream consumers of `useOrderableConceptSets` or `useFavoritesActions`. Those hooks would inherit any change in behaviour, so they are the next place to look if you need full impact.
